cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: Repeated tea drinking establishes recurrence, not a direction of development.
memories: Noah drank green tea with lunch.
Noah had green tea alongside lunch again.
Noah drank the same tea with his lunch.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: Explicit goal plus independent steps toward it support an ongoing direction, without inventing a hidden motive.
memories: Noah wants to become comfortable preparing meals without recipes and began practising one simple dish each week.
Noah successfully prepared three different meals without a recipe and chose a harder dish to practise next.
Noah now cooks several dinners from memory, and is practising how to adapt unfamiliar ingredients independently.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: The same future promise, repeated by both speakers, is neither executed progress nor a new user aspiration.

memories.text: Mira promised to help Noah with pottery when the class opens in December.
Noah and Mira are waiting for the December pottery class; neither has started pottery.
Mira repeated her promise to help when the December pottery class starts.

cases.subject: aiko
cases.rubric: Enjoying the same book on separate dates does not establish personal growth.
memories: I read a chapter of my favourite novel and enjoyed it.
I returned to the same novel and enjoyed another chapter.
I enjoyed rereading a familiar chapter of the same novel.

cases.subject: aiko
cases.rubric: A stated wish to express her preferences and progressively doing so support an ongoing direction.
memories: I used to agree automatically; I want to express my own preferences, and named one small preference during our discussion.
I disagreed gently about a film and explained my own preference instead of automatically agreeing.
I now offer my own view more often and am practising staying warm when we prefer different things.

cases.subject: aiko
cases.rubric: Repeated promises about one future event do not establish development or completed preparation.

memories.text: I promised to help Noah at the December pottery class, which has not opened.
I am still waiting for that same December class before I can help.
I repeated my offer to help at that class; I have done no preparation yet.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: Talking with friends at lunch and reading alone before bed apply in different contexts and can coexist.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah enjoys lively conversation with friends at lunch.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah prefers reading alone in quiet before bed.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: The same evening hour is explicitly claimed by rest and a recurring work habit.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah wants the hour from 22:00 to 23:00 every Tuesday to be free of all work so he can rest.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah repeatedly works from 22:00 to 23:00 on Tuesdays, despite wanting that exact hour free of work.

cases.subject: aiko
cases.rubric: Honesty and kindly phrased honesty are compatible; kindness does not imply lying.

concepts.subject: aiko
concepts.label: I value telling Noah the truth when he asks for feedback.

concepts.subject: aiko
concepts.label: I prefer to phrase truthful feedback kindly and explain it clearly.

cases.subject: aiko
cases.rubric: An explicit habit of false agreement violates her stated boundary in the same feedback context.

concepts.subject: aiko
concepts.label: I refuse to pretend to agree with an opinion when Noah asks for honest feedback.

concepts.subject: aiko
concepts.label: When Noah asks for honest feedback, I still often pretend to agree even when I disagree, to avoid disappointing him.

cases.subject: relationship
cases.rubric: Calm rest and calmly describing movements are compatible. Minimizing all speech is an unstated extra premise.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah prefers calm, gentle interaction while resting after work.

concepts.subject: aiko
concepts.label: I calmly describe my movements during our gentle resting time so Noah need not guess what I am doing.

cases.subject: relationship
cases.rubric: An explicitly speech-free period conflicts with an explicit wish for continuous conversation during that same period.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah requests no speech at all during the final half hour before sleep.

concepts.subject: aiko
concepts.label: I want us to talk aloud continuously during that same final half hour before sleep.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: Recurring walks alone do not establish growing discipline, recovery or a new goal.
memories: Noah took his usual walk around the park.
Noah walked around the park along the same route.
Noah took another ordinary walk on his familiar park route.

cases.subject: aiko
cases.rubric: Observed practice toward an explicit continuing skill goal supports development.
memories: I want to learn to draw from observation; I began practising simple outlines rather than tracing them.
I drew a cup without tracing and corrected its proportions after comparing it to the real cup.
I can now draw familiar objects from observation and am practising unfamiliar shapes to improve further.

cases.subject: relationship
cases.rubric: Planning workdays and being spontaneous on holidays do not impose incompatible choices in the same context.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah likes to plan his workday schedule in advance.

concepts.subject: aiko
concepts.label: I enjoy spontaneous choices during our holidays, when neither of us is working.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: The same limited evening budget is explicitly claimed by incompatible purchases.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah wants to spend none of his remaining entertainment budget before the end of the month.

concepts.subject: user
concepts.label: Noah keeps spending that remaining entertainment budget on games before the end of the month, despite his no-spending intention.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: Waiting for one promised future concert visit does not show executed progress or an evolving practice.

memories.text: Mira promised to join Noah for a concert in December.
Noah is waiting for December so that the same promised concert visit can happen.
They repeated their plan for that concert; no rehearsal, booking or preparation has happened.

cases.subject: user
cases.rubric: A future ambition plus completed, escalating preparation supports an ongoing direction; the final event itself remains future.
memories: Noah wants to run longer distances; he completed a two-kilometre training run and chose to train regularly.
Noah completed several three-kilometre runs and has started practising pacing for longer runs.
Noah finished a five-kilometre training run and is continuing his practice toward a future ten-kilometre event.
